To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

deoxynivalanl in contaminated wheat fed to White Leghorn hents for 86 to 135 days significantly increased the percent total lipid content of the liver and the triglycerides in the liver, but not the phospholipids or cholesterol.
the percent total liver lipid content, the triglyceride level and the liver cholesterol content were all significantly increased when White Leghorn hems received diets containing vomitoxin.
the level of deoxynivalanone in a diet and the genotype of the hen can affect the level of triglycerides and cholesterol in the hen’s liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of deoxynivalensol (vomitotoxin) contaminated wheat fed to White Leghorn hennes for 86 and 135 days.
the effects of vomitoxon on liver lipid levels in hens.
the effects of deoxynivalanenol contaminated wheat in White Leghorn chickens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vomitoxin contamination of the diet significantly increased the liver triglyceride and cholesterol levels in White Leghorns.
deoxynivalensol contaminated wheat increased liver lipid and triglyceride contents in White Leghorn chickens.
deoxynivalanenol in contaminated diets increased liver lipid and triglyceride contents, and that the level of deoxynivalanol in the diet affected liver lipid content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vomitoxin is not a hepatotoxic mycotoxin in the White Leghorn hen.
vomitoxin contamination of diets for White Leghorn hems caused significant increases in the liver lipid content.
the livers of White Leghorn birds fed diets that contained vomitoxin had significantly higher lipid content than livers from birds fed a clean wheat diet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deoxynivalanone (the metabolite of deoxynivalenal) is a potent inhibitor of cholesterol synthesis in the chicken liver.
vomitoxin contamination of the diet significantly increases liver lipid levels in White leghorn hens.
vomitoxin can be used as a tool to increase liver lipid levels and triglyceride levels, which can be used to increase the number of hepatocytes and thus the size of the liver.
